diagram_math_checks.details: The kernel quotient in Example and Verification 1.1 is the two-bit parity quotient: H=(0,0), Ha=(1,0), Hb=(0,1), Hab=(1,1). By def-labeled-schreier-coset-graph, a flips the first bit and b the second. The eight depicted edges are H→Ha (a), Ha→H (a), H→Hb (b), Hb→H (b), Ha→Hab (b), Hab→Ha (b), Hab→Hb (a), Hb→Hab (a). Each source/target is therefore correct.

Each of the four vertices has one outgoing a-edge and one outgoing b-edge and likewise one incoming edge of each label, total eight positive directed edges. Opposite positive arrows are different graph edges, not a single edge with reverse interpretation. Backward traversal of an individual x-edge reads x^{-1}, matching the local definition. Actual native image shows all eight arrows and arrowheads, including both bottom a-edges; no cycle shorthand is used.

The three solid arrows are exactly the displayed tree from the Example: H→Ha (a), H→Hb (b), Ha→Hab (b). They connect all four vertices with three edges and no undirected cycle. The unique paths from H yield representatives 1,a,b,ab, agreeing with Verification 2.1 and lem-spanning-trees-and-schreier-systems-correspond.

Using s(t,x)=tx(overline{tx})^{-1} from the theorem supplier chain (lem-tree-schreier-generators-are-freely-independent, Fact L2), (1) Ha→H has (t,x,u)=(a,a,1) and word a²; (2) Hb→H has (b,b,1) and b²; (3) Hab→Ha has (ab,b,a) and ab²a⁻¹; (4) Hab→Hb has (ab,a,b) and abab⁻¹; (5) Hb→Hab has (b,a,ab) and bab⁻¹a⁻¹. These match exactly the original basis and Verification 2.1. The three tree edges yield the identity.

The original Example, all Facts, and Verification steps 1.1–3.1 are byte-preserved. The final Remarks explicitly say that verification is independent of the illustration. No new assumptions, logical suppliers, or claim changes are introduced.
